verses.text: Theophilus, in my first book I wrote about everything Jesus began to do and teach
until the day he was taken up to heaven. Before that, through the Holy Spirit, he gave instructions to the apostles he had chosen.
After he suffered, he showed them in many convincing ways that he was alive. Over forty days he appeared to them and spoke about God’s Kingdom.
While he was gathered with them, he told them, “Don’t leave Jerusalem. Wait for what the Father promised—the promise you heard me talk about.
“John baptized with water, but in just a few days you will be baptized with the Holy Spirit.”
When they met together, they asked him, “Lord, are you going to restore the kingdom to Israel now?”
He replied, “You don’t need to know the dates or times the Father has set by his own authority.
“But you will receive power when the Holy Spirit comes on you. You will be my witnesses in Jerusalem, throughout Judea and Samaria, and to the ends of the earth.”
After saying this, he was lifted up as they watched, and a cloud took him out of their sight.
They kept staring into the sky as he went. Suddenly, two men dressed in white stood beside them
and said, “Men of Galilee, why are you standing here looking into the sky? This Jesus, who was taken up from you into heaven, will come back in the same way you saw him go.”
Then they returned to Jerusalem from the hill called Olivet, which is near the city, about a Sabbath day’s walk away.

When they arrived, they went upstairs to the room where they were staying. Those there were Peter, John, James, Andrew, Philip, Thomas, Bartholomew, Matthew, James son of Alphaeus, Simon the Zealot, and Judas son of James.
They all kept meeting together in prayer, along with the women, Mary the mother of Jesus, and his brothers.
During those days, Peter stood up among the believers—about 120 people were gathered—and said,
“Brothers and sisters, Scripture had to be fulfilled. The Holy Spirit spoke through David about Judas, who led the people who arrested Jesus.
“He was counted as one of us and shared in this ministry.”
“With the money he got for his wickedness, Judas bought a field. He fell headfirst, his body split open, and his insides spilled out.
“Everyone living in Jerusalem heard about it, so in their language they called that field Akeldama, meaning ‘Field of Blood.’
“The Psalms say, ‘Let his home become deserted; let no one live there,’ and, ‘Let someone else take his position.’
“So we need to choose one of the men who accompanied us the whole time the Lord Jesus lived among us,
“from the time John baptized people until the day Jesus was taken up from us. One of them must join us as a witness to his resurrection.”
They put forward two men: Joseph called Barsabbas, also known as Justus, and Matthias.
They prayed, “Lord, you know everyone’s heart. Show us which of these two you have chosen
“to take this ministry and apostleship that Judas left to go where he belongs.”
Then they cast lots, and the lot chose Matthias. He was added to the eleven apostles.
When the day of Pentecost arrived, they were all together in one place.
Suddenly a sound like a powerful wind came from heaven and filled the whole house where they were sitting.
They saw what looked like tongues of fire spreading out and resting on each of them.
They were all filled with the Holy Spirit and began speaking in other languages as the Spirit enabled them.
At that time, devout Jews from every nation under heaven were living in Jerusalem.
When they heard the sound, a crowd gathered, completely confused, because each person heard them speaking in their own language.
They were amazed and wondered, saying, “Aren’t all these people speaking Galileans?
“So how are we each hearing our own native language?
“We’re Parthians, Medes, Elamites, and people from Mesopotamia, Judea, Cappadocia, Pontus, and Asia,
“Phrygia, Pamphylia, Egypt, and the parts of Libya near Cyrene. Some of us are visitors from Rome, both Jews and converts to Judaism;
“and some are Cretans and Arabs. Yet we hear them speaking in our own languages about the mighty works of God!”
They were all amazed and puzzled, asking one another, “What does this mean?”
Others made fun of them and said, “They’ve had too much new wine.”
Peter stood up with the eleven, raised his voice, and addressed them: “People of Judea and everyone living in Jerusalem, listen closely to what I’m telling you.
“These people aren’t drunk, as you think. It’s only nine in the morning!
“What you’re seeing is what the prophet Joel spoke about:
“‘God says: In the last days I will pour out my Spirit on all people. Your sons and daughters will prophesy; your young men will see visions, and your elders will dream dreams.
“‘In those days I will pour out my Spirit on my male and female servants, and they will prophesy.
“‘I will show wonders in the sky above and signs on the earth below: blood, fire, and clouds of smoke.
“‘The sun will turn dark and the moon red like blood before the Lord’s great and glorious day arrives.
“‘Everyone who calls on the Lord’s name will be saved.’
“People of Israel, listen to this: Jesus of Nazareth was a man God showed you was from him through powerful works, wonders, and signs—which God did among you, as you know.
“He was handed over according to God’s set plan and foreknowledge. You used lawless people to nail him to a cross and kill him.
“But God raised him up and freed him from death’s agony, because death couldn’t hold on to him.
“David said about him: ‘I always saw the Lord before me. He is at my right hand, so I won’t be shaken.
“‘That’s why my heart is glad and my words are full of joy. My body, too, will live in hope,
“‘because you will not abandon me to the grave or let your Holy One decay.
“‘You have shown me the paths of life; your presence fills me with joy.’
“Brothers and sisters, I can speak plainly about our ancestor David: he died, was buried, and his tomb is still here with us.
“He was a prophet and knew God had sworn to him that one of his descendants, in human lineage, would sit on his throne.
“David saw ahead and spoke about the Messiah’s resurrection: he would not be left among the dead, and his body would not decay.
“God raised this Jesus to life, and all of us are witnesses.
“Now exalted to God’s right hand, he received the promised Holy Spirit from the Father and has poured out what you now see and hear.
“David himself did not go up to heaven, but he says: ‘The Lord said to my Lord, “Sit at my right hand
“‘“until I put your enemies under your feet.”’
“So all Israel should know for certain that God has made this Jesus, whom you crucified, both Lord and Messiah.”
When the people heard this, it hit them hard. They asked Peter and the other apostles, “Brothers, what should we do?”
Peter told them, “Turn back to God, and each of you be baptized in the name of Jesus Christ for the forgiveness of your sins. Then you will receive the gift of the Holy Spirit.
“This promise is for you, your children, and everyone far away—for all whom the Lord our God calls to himself.”
With many other words Peter warned them and urged them, “Be saved from this corrupt generation!”
Those who gladly accepted his message were baptized. About three thousand people were added that day.
They devoted themselves to the apostles’ teaching, to fellowship, to sharing meals, and to prayer.
Everyone was filled with awe, and the apostles performed many wonders and signs.
All the believers stayed together and shared everything they had.
They sold their possessions and belongings and distributed the money to anyone who needed help.
Every day they met together at the temple. They shared meals in their homes with glad and sincere hearts.
They praised God and had the goodwill of all the people. And day by day the Lord added to their community those who were being saved.
One day Peter and John were going up to the temple at three in the afternoon, the hour of prayer.
A man who had been unable to walk since birth was being carried there. Every day people set him down by the temple gate called Beautiful so he could ask for help from those going in.
When he saw Peter and John about to enter the temple, he asked them for money.
Peter looked straight at him, as did John, and said, “Look at us.”
The man paid close attention, expecting to get something from them.
Peter said, “I don’t have silver or gold, but I’ll give you what I do have. In the name of Jesus Christ of Nazareth, get up and walk!”
Peter took him by the right hand and helped him up. Immediately his feet and ankles became strong.
He jumped to his feet and began walking. Then he went into the temple with them, walking, jumping, and praising God.
Everyone saw him walking and praising God.
They recognized him as the man who used to sit begging for help at the Beautiful Gate. They were amazed and stunned by what had happened to him.
As the man who had been healed held on to Peter and John, all the people hurried over to them at the place called Solomon’s Porch, amazed.
When Peter saw this, he addressed the people: “People of Israel, why are you so amazed? Why are you staring at us as if our own power or devotion made this man walk?
“The God of Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob—the God of our ancestors—has honored his servant Jesus. You handed him over and rejected him in Pilate’s presence, even though Pilate had decided to release him.
“You rejected the Holy and Righteous One and asked for a murderer to be released instead.
“You killed the source of life, but God raised him from the dead. We are witnesses of this.
“Through faith in Jesus’ name, this man—whom you see and know—was made strong. Faith in Jesus has made him completely well, as you can all see.
“Brothers and sisters, I know you and your leaders acted without understanding.
“But this is how God fulfilled what he had announced through all the prophets: the Messiah would suffer.
“So turn back to God and change direction, so your sins may be wiped away and refreshing times may come from the Lord.
“Then he will send Jesus, the Messiah appointed for you,
“whom heaven must receive until the time comes to restore everything, as God announced long ago through his holy prophets.
“Moses said, ‘The Lord God will raise up a prophet for you from among your own people, like me. Listen to everything he tells you.
“‘Anyone who refuses to listen to that prophet will be completely removed from the people.’
“All the prophets, from Samuel onward, who spoke also announced these days.
“You are the children of the prophets and of the covenant God made with your ancestors when he told Abraham, ‘Through your offspring all the families of the earth will be blessed.’
“God raised up his servant and sent him to you first, to bless you by turning each of you away from your evil ways.”
While Peter and John were speaking to the people, the priests, the temple guard captain, and the Sadducees came up to them.
They were upset because the apostles were teaching the people and announcing that the dead are raised through Jesus.
They arrested Peter and John and kept them in custody until the next day, since it was already evening.
But many who heard the message believed, and the number of the men grew to about five thousand.
The next morning, Jerusalem’s rulers, elders, and scribes gathered together.
The high priest Annas was there, along with Caiaphas, John, Alexander, and others from the high priest’s family.
They brought Peter and John in front of them and asked, “By what power or in whose name did you do this?”
Then Peter, filled with the Holy Spirit, said to them, “Rulers and elders of the people,
“if we’re being questioned today about the good done for a man who couldn’t walk, and how he was healed,
“then all of you and everyone in Israel should know: this man stands here healthy through the name of Jesus Christ of Nazareth, whom you crucified and whom God raised from the dead.
“Jesus is ‘the stone you builders rejected, which has become the cornerstone.’
“Salvation is found in no one else. There is no other name under heaven given to humanity by which we must be saved.”
When they saw Peter and John speaking boldly, and realized they were ordinary, untrained men, they were amazed. They also recognized that the two had been with Jesus.
They could see the healed man standing there with them, so they had nothing to say against it.
They ordered Peter and John to leave the council room and then discussed the matter among themselves.
They said, “What are we going to do with these men? Everyone in Jerusalem knows they performed a clear miracle, and we can’t deny it.
“But to keep this from spreading any further among the people, let’s threaten them so they won’t speak to anyone in this name again.”
They called Peter and John back and ordered them not to speak or teach at all in the name of Jesus.
But Peter and John replied, “You decide whether it is right in God’s sight to obey you instead of God.
“We can’t keep quiet about what we have seen and heard.”
After threatening them some more, the leaders let them go. They couldn’t find a way to punish them because the people were praising God for what had happened.
The man who had been miraculously healed was over forty years old.
After their release, Peter and John went back to their group and reported everything the chief priests and elders had said.
When the others heard, they raised their voices together in prayer to God: “Lord, you made the sky, the earth, the sea, and everything in them.
“Through the mouth of your servant David, you said: ‘Why are the nations furious? Why do the peoples plot what is pointless?
“‘The kings of the earth take their stand, and the rulers join forces against the Lord and against his Messiah.’
“That is what happened here: Herod and Pontius Pilate joined with the Gentiles and the people of Israel against your holy servant Jesus, whom you anointed.
“They did what your power and plan had already decided would happen.
“Now, Lord, notice their threats and help your servants speak your word with complete boldness.
“Reach out your hand to heal, and let signs and wonders happen through the name of your holy servant Jesus.”
After they prayed, the place where they were gathered shook. They were all filled with the Holy Spirit and spoke God’s word boldly.
The whole group of believers was united in heart and purpose. No one claimed their possessions as only their own; they shared everything.
With great power, the apostles testified that the Lord Jesus had risen. God’s grace was strongly at work among them all.
No one among them was in need. Those who owned land or houses sold them and brought the money from the sales
and placed it at the apostles’ feet. It was then distributed to each person according to their need.
One of them was Joses, a Levite from Cyprus. The apostles called him Barnabas, which means “Son of Encouragement.”
He owned a field, sold it, and brought the money and placed it at the apostles’ feet.
A man named Ananias, along with his wife Sapphira, sold some property.
He secretly kept some of the money for himself, and his wife knew about it. He brought the rest and placed it at the apostles’ feet.
Peter said, “Ananias, why did Satan fill your heart so you would lie to the Holy Spirit and keep some of the land’s money?
“Before you sold it, wasn’t it yours? And after you sold it, wasn’t the money yours to do with as you wished? Why did you plan this in your heart? You haven’t lied to people; you have lied to God.”
When Ananias heard this, he fell down and died. Great fear came over everyone who heard about it.
Some young men got up, wrapped his body, carried him out, and buried him.
About three hours later, his wife came in, not knowing what had happened.
Peter asked her, “Tell me, did you sell the land for this amount?” She answered, “Yes, that was the price.”
Peter said to her, “How could the two of you agree to test the Lord’s Spirit? Listen—the people who buried your husband are at the door, and they’ll carry you out too.”
At once she fell down at his feet and died. The young men came in, found her dead, carried her out, and buried her beside her husband.
Great fear came over the whole church and everyone who heard about these events.
The apostles performed many signs and wonders among the people. The believers met together at Solomon’s Porch.
The others didn’t dare join them, but the people spoke highly of them.
More and more believers—both men and women—were added to the Lord.
People even carried the sick into the streets and laid them on beds and mats, hoping that Peter’s shadow might fall on some of them as he passed by.
Crowds also came from the towns around Jerusalem, bringing sick people and those troubled by unclean spirits. They were all healed.
Then the high priest and everyone with him, who belonged to the Sadducees, stood up, filled with jealousy.
They arrested the apostles and put them in the public jail.
But during the night, an angel of the Lord opened the jail doors, led them out, and said,
“Go stand in the temple and tell the people everything about this new life.”

They heard him and entered the temple around daybreak to teach. Meanwhile, the high priest and his associates called the council together, along with all the elders of Israel, and sent for the prisoners.
But when the officers arrived at the jail, they didn’t find the apostles there. They returned and reported,
“We found the jail securely locked and the guards standing at the doors. But when we opened them, no one was inside.”
When the captain of the temple guard and the chief priests heard this report, they were confused and wondered what would happen next.
Then someone came in and told them, “The men you put in jail are in the temple, standing there and teaching the people.”
The captain went with the officers and brought the apostles back, but without force, because they were afraid the people would stone them.
They brought the apostles in and stood them before the council. The high priest questioned them:
“We strictly ordered you not to teach in this name! And look—you’ve filled Jerusalem with your teaching and want to make us responsible for this man’s blood.”
Peter and the other apostles answered, “We must obey God rather than people.
“The God of our ancestors raised Jesus to life—the one you killed by hanging him on a tree.
“God exalted him to his right hand as Leader and Savior, to give Israel the opportunity to turn back and receive forgiveness of sins.
“We are witnesses of these things, and so is the Holy Spirit, whom God gives to those who obey him.”
When they heard this, the council members were furious and wanted to kill the apostles.
But a Pharisee named Gamaliel stood up in the council. He was a law teacher respected by all the people. He ordered the apostles to be taken outside for a little while.
Then he said, “People of Israel, think carefully about what you’re about to do to these men.
“Some time ago Theudas appeared, claiming to be someone important. About four hundred men joined him. He was killed, and all his followers scattered and came to nothing.
“After him, Judas from Galilee appeared during the census and led some people away with him. He also died, and all his followers were scattered.
“So here’s my advice: leave these men alone. If their plan or work comes from people, it will fail.
“But if it comes from God, you won’t be able to stop them—and you might end up fighting against God.” They accepted his advice.
They called the apostles back, had them beaten, ordered them not to speak in Jesus’ name, and released them.
The apostles left the council, glad that God had counted them worthy to suffer shame for Jesus’ name.
Every day, in the temple and in people’s homes, they kept teaching and announcing that Jesus is the Messiah.
As the number of disciples kept growing, the Greek-speaking believers complained against the Hebrew-speaking believers because their widows were being overlooked in the daily food distribution.
The Twelve called all the disciples together and said, “It wouldn’t be right for us to stop teaching God’s word so we can manage the food service.
“So, brothers and sisters, choose seven respected men from among you, full of the Spirit and wisdom. We’ll put them in charge of this work.
“Then we can keep giving ourselves to prayer and to serving through the word.”
This proposal pleased everyone. They chose Stephen, a man full of faith and the Holy Spirit; Philip, Prochorus, Nicanor, Timon, Parmenas, and Nicolaus, a convert from Antioch.
They brought these men to the apostles, who prayed and laid their hands on them.
God’s word continued to spread, and the number of disciples in Jerusalem grew rapidly. A large number of priests also accepted the faith.
Stephen, full of grace and power, performed great wonders and signs among the people.
But some people from the synagogue called the Freedmen—including people from Cyrene, Alexandria, Cilicia, and Asia—started arguing with Stephen.
They couldn’t stand up to the wisdom and the Spirit with which he spoke.
So they secretly persuaded some men to claim, “We heard him speak against Moses and God.”
They stirred up the people, elders, and scribes, then came after Stephen, seized him, and brought him before the council.
They brought in false witnesses, who said, “This man is always speaking against this holy place and the law.
“We heard him say that Jesus of Nazareth will destroy this place and change the customs Moses handed down to us.”
Everyone sitting in the council stared at Stephen and saw that his face looked like an angel’s.
The high priest asked Stephen, “Are these accusations true?”
Stephen replied, “Brothers and fathers, hear me. The glorious God appeared to our ancestor Abraham while he was still in Mesopotamia, before he settled in Haran.
“God told him, ‘Leave your land and your relatives. Go to the land I will show you.’
“So Abraham left the Chaldeans’ land and settled in Haran. After his father died, God brought him here, to the land where you now live.
“God gave him no inheritance here—not even enough ground to stand on. But God promised to give the land to him and to his descendants, even though Abraham had no child yet.
“God told him that his descendants would live as foreigners in another land, where people would enslave and mistreat them for four hundred years.
“God also said, ‘I will judge the nation that enslaves them. Afterward they will leave and worship me in this place.’

“Then God gave Abraham the covenant of circumcision. Abraham became Isaac’s father and circumcised him on the eighth day. Isaac became Jacob’s father, and Jacob became the father of the twelve patriarchs.
“The patriarchs were jealous of Joseph and sold him into Egypt. But God was with him
“and rescued him from all his troubles. God gave him favor and wisdom before Pharaoh, Egypt’s king, who appointed him governor over Egypt and his whole household.
“Then a famine and severe hardship struck all Egypt and Canaan, and our ancestors couldn’t find food.
“When Jacob heard there was grain in Egypt, he sent our ancestors there for the first time.
“When they went a second time, Joseph revealed who he was to his brothers, and Pharaoh learned about Joseph’s family.
“Joseph sent for his father Jacob and all his relatives—seventy-five people in all.
“Jacob went down to Egypt, where he and our ancestors died.
“They were brought back to Shechem and placed in the tomb Abraham had bought with silver from Hamor’s family in Shechem.
“As the time drew near for God to fulfill his promise to Abraham, our people had become numerous in Egypt.
“Then a new king came to power, one who knew nothing about Joseph.
“He took advantage of our people and cruelly mistreated our ancestors, forcing them to abandon their babies so they wouldn’t survive.
“At that time Moses was born. He was exceptionally beautiful before God and was cared for at his father’s home for three months.
“When he was left outside, Pharaoh’s daughter took him in and raised him as her own son.
“Moses was taught all the wisdom of the Egyptians and became powerful in what he said and did.
“When Moses was forty, he decided to visit his fellow Israelites.
“He saw one of them being mistreated, stepped in to defend him, and struck down the Egyptian who was hurting him.
“Moses thought his people would understand that God was using him to rescue them, but they didn’t.
“The next day he saw two Israelites fighting. He tried to make peace, saying, ‘Men, you’re brothers. Why are you hurting each other?’
“But the man harming his neighbor pushed Moses away and said, ‘Who put you in charge of us as ruler and judge?
“‘Are you going to kill me like you killed the Egyptian yesterday?’
“When Moses heard that, he fled and lived as a foreigner in Midian, where he had two sons.
“Forty years later, an angel of the Lord appeared to him in the wilderness near Mount Sinai, in the flame of a burning bush.
“Moses was amazed by what he saw. As he came closer to look, the Lord’s voice spoke to him:
“‘I am the God of your ancestors—the God of Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob.’ Moses trembled and didn’t dare look.
“The Lord told him, ‘Take off your sandals. The place where you’re standing is holy ground.
“‘I have seen how my people are suffering in Egypt. I have heard their groaning, and I have come down to rescue them. Now come—I’m sending you to Egypt.’
“This is the same Moses whom the people rejected by asking, ‘Who made you ruler and judge?’ God sent him as both ruler and rescuer, with the help of the angel who appeared to him in the bush.
“He led them out, performing wonders and signs in Egypt, at the Red Sea, and in the wilderness for forty years.
“This is the Moses who told the Israelites, ‘God will raise up a prophet like me for you from among your own people.’
“He was with our people in the wilderness assembly, with the angel who spoke to him at Mount Sinai and with our ancestors. He received living words to pass on to us.
“But our ancestors refused to obey him. They pushed him away and turned their hearts back toward Egypt.
“They told Aaron, ‘Make gods to lead us. We don’t know what happened to this Moses who brought us out of Egypt.’
“They made a calf idol in those days, offered sacrifices to it, and celebrated what their own hands had made.

“So God turned away from them and let them worship the stars in the sky, just as the prophets’ book says: ‘People of Israel, did you bring me offerings and sacrifices during those forty years in the wilderness?
“‘You carried the shrine of Moloch and the star of your god Rephan, idols you made to worship. So I will send you into exile beyond Babylon.’
“Our ancestors had the tent of the covenant in the wilderness. God had instructed Moses to make it according to the pattern he had seen.
“Our ancestors received the tent from those who came before them and brought it with Joshua when they took possession of the nations God drove out ahead of them. It stayed there until David’s time.
“David found favor with God and asked to build a dwelling place for the God of Jacob.
“But Solomon built a house for him.
“Still, the Most High doesn’t live in houses built by human hands. As the prophet says:
“‘Heaven is my throne, and the earth is under my feet. What kind of house could you build for me?’ says the Lord. ‘Where could I rest?
“‘Didn’t I make all these things with my own hand?’
“You are stubborn, with hearts and ears that are uncircumcised! You always resist the Holy Spirit, just as your ancestors did.
“Which prophet did your ancestors not persecute? They killed those who announced the coming of the Righteous One. And now you have betrayed and murdered him.
“You received the law delivered by angels, but you haven’t kept it!”
When the council heard this, they were furious and ground their teeth at Stephen.
But Stephen, filled with the Holy Spirit, looked up into heaven and saw God’s glory, with Jesus standing at God’s right hand.
He said, “Look! I see heaven opened, and the Son of Man standing at God’s right hand!”
They shouted loudly, covered their ears, and rushed at Stephen together.
They dragged him outside the city and stoned him. The witnesses laid their coats at the feet of a young man named Saul.
As they stoned Stephen, he called out, “Lord Jesus, receive my spirit!”
He knelt and cried out loudly, “Lord, don’t hold this sin against them!” After saying this, he died.
Saul approved of Stephen’s execution. That day, a fierce wave of persecution hit the Jerusalem church, and everyone except the apostles scattered through Judea and Samaria. 🌪️
Some devout men buried Stephen and mourned him deeply. 😢
Saul was tearing the church apart. He went house to house, dragging both men and women off to prison. ⛓️
But the believers who scattered kept going, sharing God’s message wherever they went. 📣
Philip went down to a city in Samaria and announced the Christ to its people. ✨
The crowds listened closely to Philip. They heard his message and saw the signs he performed, all together in one response. 👂
Unclean spirits came out of many people, crying loudly as they left. Many who were paralyzed or unable to walk were healed too. 🙌
That city was filled with joy. 🎉
A man named Simon had been practicing magic in the city for a while. He amazed the people of Samaria and made himself out to be somebody important. 🎩
Everyone, from the least to the greatest, listened to him. They said, “This man is the great power of God.” 👀
They had listened to him for a long time because his magic kept amazing them. 🪄
But when they believed Philip preaching the Good News about God’s Kingdom and the name of Jesus Christ, men and women were baptized. 💧
Simon himself believed and was baptized. He stayed close to Philip, amazed by the signs and powerful miracles he saw. 😮
The apostles in Jerusalem heard that Samaria had welcomed God’s message, so they sent Peter and John there. 📩
When they arrived, they prayed for the believers to receive the Holy Spirit. 🙏
The Holy Spirit had not yet come upon any of them; they had only been baptized in the name of Christ Jesus. 💧
Then Peter and John laid their hands on them, and they received the Holy Spirit. 🔥
Simon saw that the Spirit was given when the apostles laid hands on people, so he offered them money. 🪙
He said, “Give me this power too, so anyone I lay hands on can receive the Holy Spirit.” 💰
Peter answered, “May your money perish with you! You thought God’s gift could be bought with cash. ⚠️
“You have no share in this work. Your heart is not right with God. 💔
“Turn away from this evil and ask the Lord to forgive what you were thinking. 🙏
“I can see bitterness has poisoned you, and wrongdoing has you locked up.” ⛓️
Simon answered, “Please pray to the Lord for me, so none of what you said happens to me.” 😟
After testifying and sharing the Lord’s message, the apostles headed back to Jerusalem. On the way, they preached the Good News in many Samaritan villages. 📣
An angel of the Lord told Philip, “Get up and go south, to the road from Jerusalem down to Gaza.” That road crossed the desert. 🏜️
Philip went. There he met an Ethiopian eunuch, a high official in charge of the treasury of Candace, the queen of Ethiopia. He had gone to Jerusalem to worship. 👑
Now he was on his way home, riding in his chariot and reading the prophet Isaiah. 📜
The Spirit told Philip, “Go over and stay near that chariot.” 🛞
Philip ran up and heard him reading Isaiah. He asked, “Do you understand what you are reading?” 📖
The man replied, “How can I, unless someone guides me?” He invited Philip to climb up and sit with him. 🤝
The passage he was reading said: “He was led like a sheep to be slaughtered. Like a lamb quiet in front of the person shearing it, he did not open his mouth. 🐑
“In his humiliation, justice was denied him. Who can tell the story of his descendants? His life was taken from the earth.” 📜
The eunuch asked Philip, “Tell me, who is the prophet talking about—himself or someone else?” ❓
Philip began with that very passage and told him the Good News about Jesus. ✨
As they traveled, they came to some water. The eunuch said, “Look, water! Is anything stopping me from being baptized?” 💧
He told the chariot driver to stop. Philip and the eunuch both went down into the water, and Philip baptized him. 🌊
When they came up out of the water, the Spirit of the Lord suddenly took Philip away. The eunuch did not see him again, but continued on his way full of joy. 🙌
Philip appeared at Azotus. He kept sharing the Good News in every city along the way until he reached Caesarea. 📣
Saul was still threatening the Lord’s disciples with violence and death. He went to the high priest
and asked for letters to the synagogues in Damascus. He wanted permission to arrest anyone he found following the Way, men or women, and bring them bound to Jerusalem.
As he traveled and neared Damascus, a light from heaven suddenly flashed around him.
He fell to the ground and heard a voice say, “Saul, Saul, why are you persecuting me?”
He asked, “Who are you, Lord?” The Lord said, “I am Jesus, the one you are persecuting.
“Now get up and go into the city. There you’ll be told what you must do.”
The men traveling with him stood there speechless. They heard the voice but saw no one.
Saul got up from the ground. When he opened his eyes, he couldn’t see anything, so they led him by the hand into Damascus.
For three days he couldn’t see, and he neither ate nor drank.
There was a disciple in Damascus named Ananias. The Lord called to him in a vision, “Ananias!” He answered, “Here I am, Lord.”
The Lord told him, “Get up and go to the street called Straight. At the house of Judas, ask for a man from Tarsus named Saul. He is praying right now.
“In a vision he has seen a man named Ananias come in and lay hands on him so that he can see again.”
Ananias replied, “Lord, I’ve heard from many people about all the harm this man has done to your holy people in Jerusalem.
“He has authority from the chief priests here to arrest everyone who calls on your name.”
But the Lord told him, “Go. I have chosen him to carry my name before the nations, their kings, and the people of Israel.
“I will show him how much he must suffer for my name.”
Ananias went to the house and laid his hands on Saul. He said, “Brother Saul, the Lord Jesus, who appeared to you on the road here, sent me so you can see again and be filled with the Holy Spirit.”
At once something like scales fell from Saul’s eyes, and he could see again. He got up and was baptized.
He ate and regained his strength. Saul stayed several days with the disciples in Damascus.
Right away he began preaching in the synagogues that Jesus is the Son of God.
Everyone who heard him was amazed. They said, “Isn’t this the man who attacked those in Jerusalem who call on this name? Didn’t he come here to arrest them and take them to the chief priests?”
But Saul grew stronger and left the Jews living in Damascus confused, proving that Jesus is the Messiah.
After many days, the Jews plotted together to kill him.
Saul learned about their plan. They watched the city gates day and night, hoping to kill him.
But his disciples took him by night and lowered him in a basket through an opening in the city wall.
When Saul arrived in Jerusalem, he tried to join the disciples, but they were all afraid of him and didn’t believe he was a disciple.
Then Barnabas brought him to the apostles and explained how Saul had seen the Lord on the road, how the Lord had spoken to him, and how Saul had boldly preached in Jesus’ name in Damascus.
So Saul stayed with them and moved freely around Jerusalem,
speaking boldly in the name of the Lord Jesus. He argued with the Greek-speaking Jews, who then tried to kill him.
When the believers found out, they took him to Caesarea and sent him off to Tarsus.
Then the churches throughout Judea, Galilee, and Samaria had peace and grew stronger. They lived in reverence for the Lord and in the Holy Spirit’s comfort, and their numbers increased.
As Peter traveled through the region, he also visited the holy people living in Lydda.
There he met a man named Aeneas, who had been paralyzed and bedridden for eight years.
Peter said to him, “Aeneas, Jesus Christ heals you. Get up and make your bed.” At once he got up.
Everyone living in Lydda and Sharon saw him and turned to the Lord.
In Joppa there was a disciple named Tabitha, which means Dorcas. She was always doing good and helping people in need.
Around that time she became sick and died. They washed her body and laid her in an upstairs room.
Since Lydda was near Joppa, the disciples heard Peter was there. They sent two men to him, urging him, “Please come to us right away.”
Peter got up and went with them. When he arrived, they took him upstairs. All the widows stood around him crying and showing him the tunics and other clothes Dorcas had made while she was with them.
Peter sent everyone out, knelt down, and prayed. Then he turned toward the body and said, “Tabitha, get up!” She opened her eyes, saw Peter, and sat up.
He gave her his hand and helped her stand. Then he called the holy people and the widows and presented her alive.
News of this spread throughout Joppa, and many people believed in the Lord.
Peter stayed in Joppa for many days with a tanner named Simon.
In Caesarea there was a man named Cornelius, a centurion in the Italian Regiment.
He was devoted to God, as was his whole household. He gave generously to people in need and prayed to God regularly.
Around three in the afternoon, he clearly saw an angel of God come to him in a vision and call, “Cornelius!”
Cornelius stared at him in fear and asked, “What is it, sir?” The angel said, “Your prayers and gifts to the poor have risen as a reminder before God.
“Now send some men to Joppa and bring back Simon, who is also called Peter.
“He is staying with Simon the tanner, whose house is by the sea.”
After the angel left, Cornelius called two of his household servants and a devout soldier who served him regularly.
He explained everything to them and sent them to Joppa.
The next day, as they were nearing the city, Peter went up to the roof around noon to pray.
He became hungry and wanted something to eat. While the meal was being prepared, he fell into a trance.
He saw heaven open and something like a large sheet coming down to earth, lowered by its four corners.
Inside it were all kinds of four-legged animals, wild animals, reptiles, and birds.
A voice said to him, “Get up, Peter. Kill and eat.”
Peter answered, “Absolutely not, Lord! I have never eaten anything ordinary or unclean.”
The voice spoke to him a second time: “Don’t call anything unclean if God has made it clean.”
This happened three times, and then the sheet was taken back up into heaven.
Peter was puzzled about what his vision meant. Just then the men sent by Cornelius found Simon’s house and stood at the gate.
They called out and asked whether Simon, also known as Peter, was staying there.
While Peter was still thinking about the vision, the Spirit told him, “Look, three men are asking for you.
“Get up, go downstairs, and go with them without hesitation. I sent them.”
Peter went down to the men and said, “I’m the one you’re looking for. Why have you come?”

They answered, “Cornelius the centurion sent us. He’s a righteous man who honors God, and the whole Jewish nation respects him. A holy angel told him to invite you to his house and hear what you have to say.”
Peter invited them in and gave them a place to stay. The next day he set out with them, joined by some believers from Joppa.
The following day they arrived in Caesarea. Cornelius was expecting them and had gathered his relatives and close friends.
When Peter entered, Cornelius met him, fell at his feet, and bowed down to him.
But Peter helped him up and said, “Stand up. I’m only a man too.”
As Peter talked with him, he went inside and saw many people gathered there.
He said to them, “You know it’s against our law for a Jew to associate with someone from another nation or visit them. But God has shown me I must not call any person polluted or unclean.
“So when you sent for me, I came without objecting. Now tell me why you asked me to come.”
Cornelius replied, “Four days ago, at this same hour, I was praying in my house at three in the afternoon. Suddenly a man in bright clothing stood in front of me
“and said, ‘Cornelius, God has heard your prayer and remembered your gifts to the poor.
“‘Send someone to Joppa and invite Simon, also called Peter. He is staying in the home of Simon the tanner by the sea. When he arrives, he will speak to you.’
“So I sent for you right away, and it was good of you to come. Now we’re all here before God, ready to hear everything the Lord has instructed you to tell us.”
Peter began to speak: “Now I truly understand that God doesn’t play favorites.
“In every nation, anyone who honors him and does what is right is welcome to him.
“God sent his message to Israel, announcing the Good News of peace through Jesus Christ, who is Lord of all.
“You know what happened throughout Judea, beginning in Galilee after John preached baptism:
“God anointed Jesus of Nazareth with the Holy Spirit and power. He went around doing good and healing everyone oppressed by the devil, because God was with him.
“We are witnesses of everything he did in the land of the Jews and in Jerusalem. They killed him by hanging him on a tree,
“but God raised him on the third day and allowed him to be seen.
“He wasn’t shown to everyone, but to witnesses God had chosen beforehand—to us, who ate and drank with him after he rose from the dead.
“He commanded us to preach to the people and testify that God appointed him as judge of the living and the dead.
“All the prophets testify about him: everyone who believes in him receives forgiveness of sins through his name.”
While Peter was still saying this, the Holy Spirit came upon everyone who heard the message.
The Jewish believers who had come with Peter were amazed that the Holy Spirit’s gift had also been poured out on Gentiles.
They heard them speaking in other languages and praising God. Then Peter said,
“Can anyone keep these people from being baptized in water? They have received the Holy Spirit just as we have.”
So he ordered them to be baptized in the name of Jesus Christ. Then they asked him to stay with them for several days.
The apostles and the believers throughout Judea heard that Gentiles had also accepted God’s word.
When Peter came up to Jerusalem, the circumcised believers challenged him.
They said, “You went into the home of uncircumcised men and ate with them!”
So Peter began explaining the whole story to them in order:
“I was praying in Joppa and fell into a trance. I saw a vision of something like a large sheet lowered from heaven by its four corners. It came right down to me.
“I looked closely and saw four-legged animals, wild animals, reptiles, and birds.
“Then I heard a voice say, ‘Get up, Peter. Kill and eat.’
“I replied, ‘No, Lord. Nothing impure or unclean has ever gone into my mouth.’
“The voice from heaven answered a second time, ‘Don’t call unclean what God has made clean.’
“This happened three times, and then everything was taken back up into heaven.
“At that very moment, three men sent from Caesarea arrived at the house where I was staying.
“The Spirit told me to go with them without hesitation. These six brothers came with me too, and we entered the man’s house.
“He told us how he had seen an angel standing in his house, who said, ‘Send to Joppa and bring Simon, also called Peter.
“‘He will tell you a message through which you and your whole household will be saved.’
“As I began speaking, the Holy Spirit came upon them just as he came upon us at the beginning.
“Then I remembered what the Lord had said: ‘John baptized with water, but you will be baptized with the Holy Spirit.’
“If God gave them the same gift he gave us when we believed in the Lord Jesus Christ, who was I to stand in God’s way?”
When they heard this, they stopped objecting and praised God. They said, “So God has also given Gentiles the opportunity to turn to him and receive life!”
The believers scattered by the persecution that began around Stephen traveled as far as Phoenicia, Cyprus, and Antioch. They shared the message only with Jews.
But some believers from Cyprus and Cyrene went to Antioch and began telling Greek-speaking people the Good News about the Lord Jesus.
The Lord’s power was with them, and a large number believed and turned to the Lord.
News about them reached the church in Jerusalem, so they sent Barnabas to Antioch.
When he arrived and saw God’s grace at work, he was glad. He encouraged them all to stay true to the Lord with firm commitment.
Barnabas was a good man, full of the Holy Spirit and faith. Many more people came to the Lord.
Then Barnabas went to Tarsus to look for Saul.
When he found him, he brought him to Antioch. For a whole year they met with the church and taught many people. The disciples were first called Christians in Antioch.
During that time, some prophets came from Jerusalem to Antioch.
One of them, named Agabus, stood up and announced through the Spirit that a severe famine would spread across the whole world. It happened during Claudius’s reign.
So the disciples decided that each would send help to the believers living in Judea, as much as they were able.
They sent the relief to the elders through Barnabas and Saul.
Around that time, King Herod began arresting some people from the church to mistreat them.
He had James, John’s brother, killed with a sword.
When he saw that this pleased the Jews, he also arrested Peter. This happened during the Festival of Unleavened Bread.
After arresting him, Herod put him in prison and assigned four squads of four soldiers each to guard him. Herod planned to bring him out for the people after Passover.
So Peter was kept in prison, while the church prayed earnestly to God for him.
The night before Herod was to bring him out, Peter was sleeping between two soldiers, chained with two chains. Guards stood watch at the prison entrance.
Suddenly an angel of the Lord stood beside him, and a light shone in the cell. The angel tapped Peter on the side to wake him and said, “Quick, get up!” The chains fell from Peter’s hands.
The angel said, “Get dressed and put on your sandals.” Peter did. Then the angel said, “Put on your cloak and follow me.”
Peter followed him out, but he didn’t realize that what the angel was doing was real. He thought he was seeing a vision.

They passed the first and second guard posts and came to the iron gate leading into the city. It opened for them by itself. They went outside and walked down one street, then the angel suddenly left him.
When Peter came to his senses, he said, “Now I know for sure the Lord sent his angel and rescued me from Herod and from everything the Jewish people expected to happen.”
After thinking it over, he went to the home of Mary, the mother of John also called Mark. Many people were gathered there, praying.
Peter knocked at the outer gate, and a servant girl named Rhoda came to answer.
She recognized Peter’s voice and was so excited that she forgot to open the gate. She ran inside and announced that Peter was standing outside.
They said to her, “You’re out of your mind!” But she kept insisting it was true. They said, “It must be his angel.”
Meanwhile Peter kept knocking. When they opened the gate and saw him, they were stunned.

He motioned with his hand for them to be quiet and told them how the Lord had brought him out of prison. “Tell James and the other brothers and sisters,” he said. Then he left and went somewhere else.
When morning came, the soldiers were in an uproar, wondering what had happened to Peter.
Herod searched for him and couldn’t find him. He questioned the guards and ordered them executed. Then he left Judea and went down to Caesarea, where he stayed.

Herod was furious with the people of Tyre and Sidon. They came together to meet with him. After winning over Blastus, the king’s personal aide, they asked for peace because their region depended on the king’s territory for its food supply.
On the appointed day, Herod put on his royal clothes, sat on the throne, and gave a speech to them.
The crowd shouted, “That’s the voice of a god, not a human!”
At once an angel of the Lord struck Herod because he didn’t give God the glory. Worms consumed him, and he died.
But God’s word kept spreading and growing.
After completing their work, Barnabas and Saul returned from Jerusalem, bringing John, also called Mark, with them.
The church in Antioch had several prophets and teachers: Barnabas, Simeon called Niger, Lucius from Cyrene, Manaen, who had grown up with Herod the ruler, and Saul.
As they worshiped the Lord and fasted, the Holy Spirit said, “Set Barnabas and Saul apart for me for the work I’ve called them to do.”
After fasting and praying, they laid their hands on the two men and sent them off.
Sent out by the Holy Spirit, Barnabas and Saul went down to Seleucia and sailed from there to Cyprus.
In Salamis they announced God’s word in the Jewish synagogues. John was with them as their assistant.
They traveled across the island as far as Paphos, where they met a Jewish sorcerer and false prophet named Bar-Jesus.
He was with the proconsul Sergius Paulus, an intelligent man. The proconsul summoned Barnabas and Saul because he wanted to hear God’s word.
But Elymas the sorcerer—that is what his name means—opposed them and tried to turn the proconsul away from the faith.
Then Saul, also called Paul, filled with the Holy Spirit, stared directly at him
and said, “You are full of deceit and every kind of trickery, child of the devil and enemy of everything right! Will you never stop twisting the Lord’s straight paths?
“Now the Lord’s hand is against you. You will be blind for a while and won’t see the sun.” At once a mist and darkness came over him, and he went around looking for someone to guide him by the hand.
When the proconsul saw what happened, he believed. He was amazed at the Lord’s teaching.
Paul and his companions sailed from Paphos to Perga in Pamphylia. John left them there and returned to Jerusalem.
They traveled on from Perga and came to Antioch in Pisidia. On the Sabbath they went into the synagogue and sat down.
After the readings from the Law and the Prophets, the synagogue leaders sent them this message: “Brothers, if you have something encouraging for the people, please speak.”
Paul stood up, motioned with his hand, and said, “People of Israel and everyone here who honors God, listen.
“The God of Israel chose our ancestors and made our people numerous while they lived as foreigners in Egypt. Then he brought them out of Egypt with mighty power.
“For about forty years in the wilderness, he was patient with them.
“After overthrowing seven nations in Canaan, he gave our people their land as an inheritance for about 450 years.
“After that, God gave them judges until Samuel the prophet.
“Then they asked for a king, and God gave them Saul son of Kish, from the tribe of Benjamin, who ruled for forty years.
“After removing Saul, God raised up David as their king. God testified about him: ‘I have found David, Jesse’s son, a man whose heart follows mine. He will do everything I want.’
“From David’s descendants, God brought Israel a Savior, Jesus, as he had promised.
“Before Jesus came, John had already preached a baptism calling all Israel to turn back to God.
“As John finished his work, he said, ‘Who do you think I am? I’m not the one. Look, someone is coming after me, and I’m not worthy even to untie his sandals.’
“Brothers, descendants of Abraham, and all of you who honor God, this message of salvation has been sent to us.
“The people of Jerusalem and their rulers didn’t recognize Jesus or understand the prophets read every Sabbath. Yet by condemning him, they fulfilled what the prophets had said.
“They found no reason to put him to death, but still asked Pilate to have him killed.
“After they carried out everything written about him, they took him down from the tree and laid him in a tomb.
“But God raised him from the dead.
“For many days he appeared to those who had traveled with him from Galilee to Jerusalem. They are now his witnesses to the people.
“We bring you the Good News: God has fulfilled for us, their descendants, the promise he made to our ancestors.
“God fulfilled it by raising Jesus, just as the second psalm says: ‘You are my Son; today I have become your Father.’
“God raised him from the dead so that he would never decay again. He said, ‘I will give you the holy and faithful promises I made to David.’
“That’s why another psalm says, ‘You will not let your Holy One decay.’
“David served God’s purpose during his own generation, then died, was buried with his ancestors, and decayed.
“But the one God raised did not decay.
“So, brothers and sisters, know this: through Jesus forgiveness of sins is announced to you.
“Everyone who believes is made right through him in a way the Law of Moses could never accomplish.
“Be careful, then, or what the prophets spoke about may happen to you:
“‘Look, you who scoff! Be amazed and perish. I am doing something in your days that you would never believe, even if someone explained it to you.’”
As Paul and Barnabas were leaving the synagogue, the Gentiles begged them to share these words again the next Sabbath.
When the gathering ended, many Jews and devout converts followed Paul and Barnabas. The two spoke with them and urged them to keep living in God’s grace.
The next Sabbath, almost the whole city gathered to hear the Lord’s word.
When the Jews saw the crowds, jealousy took over. They opposed Paul’s words and insulted him.
Paul and Barnabas spoke boldly: “God’s word had to be spoken to you first. Since you reject it and judge yourselves unworthy of eternal life, we are turning to the Gentiles.
“For this is what the Lord commanded us: ‘I have made you a light for the nations, to bring salvation to the ends of the earth.’”
When the Gentiles heard this, they were glad and praised the Lord’s word. All who were appointed for eternal life believed.
The Lord’s message spread throughout the whole region.
But the Jews stirred up devout and influential women, along with the city’s leading men. They launched persecution against Paul and Barnabas and drove them out of the region.
They shook the dust from their feet against them and went to Iconium.
The disciples were filled with joy and the Holy Spirit.
In Iconium, Paul and Barnabas went together into the Jewish synagogue and spoke so effectively that many Jews and Greeks believed.
But the Jews who refused to believe stirred up the Gentiles and turned them against the believers.
So Paul and Barnabas stayed there a long time, speaking boldly for the Lord. The Lord confirmed his message of grace by enabling them to perform signs and wonders.
The city’s people split into two sides: some supported the Jews, others the apostles.
Then some Gentiles and Jews, together with their leaders, planned to mistreat and stone them.
When Paul and Barnabas learned about it, they fled to the Lycaonian cities of Lystra and Derbe and the surrounding area.
There they kept announcing the Good News.
In Lystra there was a man who couldn’t use his feet. He had been lame from birth and had never walked.
He listened to Paul speaking. Paul looked closely at him and saw that he had faith to be healed.
Paul called out, “Stand up straight on your feet!” The man jumped up and began walking.
When the crowd saw what Paul had done, they shouted in the Lycaonian language, “The gods have come down to us looking like people!”
They called Barnabas Jupiter and Paul Mercury, since Paul did most of the speaking.
The priest of Jupiter, whose temple stood in front of the city, brought oxen and flower garlands to the gates. He and the crowd wanted to offer sacrifices to them.
When the apostles Barnabas and Paul heard about it, they tore their clothes and rushed into the crowd, shouting:

“People, why are you doing this? We’re human beings just like you. We bring you Good News so you’ll turn away from these worthless things and turn to the living God, who made the sky, the earth, the sea, and everything in them.
“In past generations he allowed all nations to go their own way.
“Yet he never left himself without a witness: he did good, sent rain from heaven, gave fruitful seasons, and filled you with food and gladness.”
Even with these words, they could barely stop the crowd from sacrificing to them.
Then some Jews came from Antioch and Iconium and persuaded the crowd. They stoned Paul and dragged him outside the city, thinking he was dead.
But when the disciples gathered around him, he got up and went back into the city. The next day he left with Barnabas for Derbe.
After announcing the Good News in Derbe and making many disciples, they returned to Lystra, Iconium, and Antioch.
They encouraged the disciples to stay strong in the faith, saying, “We must go through many troubles to enter God’s Kingdom.”
They appointed elders for them in every church. After praying and fasting, they entrusted them to the Lord, in whom they had believed.
They traveled through Pisidia and came to Pamphylia.
After speaking the word in Perga, they went down to Attalia.
From there they sailed to Antioch, where they had first been entrusted to God’s grace for the work they had now completed.
When they arrived, they gathered the church and reported everything God had done through them, including how he had opened the door of faith to the Gentiles.
They stayed there with the disciples for a long time.
Some men came down from Judea and started teaching the believers, “Unless you are circumcised according to Moses’ custom, you cannot be saved.” ⚠️
Paul and Barnabas strongly disagreed and debated them. The church appointed them and some others to go to Jerusalem and discuss the issue with the apostles and elders. 🗣️
The church sent them on their way. As they traveled through Phoenicia and Samaria, they told how Gentiles were turning to God, bringing great joy to all the believers. 🌍
When they arrived in Jerusalem, the church, apostles, and elders welcomed them. They reported everything God had done through them. 🙌
Some believers from the Pharisee group stood up and said, “Gentiles must be circumcised and ordered to keep the Law of Moses.” 📜
The apostles and elders gathered to consider the matter. 🏛️
After a long debate, Peter stood up and said, “Brothers, you know that some time ago God chose me to share the Good News with the Gentiles, so they could hear and believe. 📣
“God, who knows the heart, showed that he accepted them by giving them the Holy Spirit, just as he did to us. 🔥
“He made no distinction between us and them. He cleansed their hearts through faith. 💛
“So why are you testing God by putting a heavy yoke on the disciples—something our ancestors and we could not carry? 🪢
“We believe we are saved through the grace of the Lord Jesus, just as they are.” 🙏
The whole crowd fell silent and listened as Barnabas and Paul told about the signs and wonders God had done among the Gentiles through them. 👂
When they finished, James answered, “Brothers, listen to me. 🗣️
“Simeon has explained how God first looked to the Gentiles, choosing from among them a people to bear his name. 🌍
“This agrees with what the prophets wrote. Scripture says: 📖
“‘After this I will return. I will rebuild David’s fallen tent. I will rebuild its ruins and set it up again, 🏚️
“‘so that the rest of humanity may seek the Lord—including all the Gentiles who are called by my name. The Lord says this, and he has been making these things known from long ago.’” ✨
“God’s works have been known to him from eternity. ⏳
“So here is my judgment: we should not make life difficult for Gentiles who are turning to God. 🤝
“Instead, let us write to them to stay away from food polluted by idols, sexual immorality, meat from strangled animals, and blood. 📝
“For Moses has been preached in every city for generations and is read in the synagogues every Sabbath.” 📜

Then the apostles and elders, together with the whole church, chose men from their group to go with Paul and Barnabas to Antioch. They chose Judas, called Barsabbas, and Silas, respected leaders among the believers. 👥
They sent this letter with them: “From the apostles, elders, and fellow believers, to the Gentile believers in Antioch, Syria, and Cilicia: greetings. ✉️
“We heard that some people from among us came and upset you with their words, troubling you and saying you must be circumcised and keep the Law. We never gave them that command. ⚠️
“So we have agreed together to choose representatives and send them to you with our dear friends Barnabas and Paul, 🤝
“who have risked their lives for the name of our Lord Jesus Christ. ✝️
“We are sending Judas and Silas too. They will tell you the same message in person. 🗣️
“The Holy Spirit and we have agreed not to place any extra burden on you beyond these essentials: 🔥
“Stay away from food offered to idols, from blood, from meat of strangled animals, and from sexual immorality. If you avoid these things, you will do well. Farewell.” 👋
The messengers left for Antioch, gathered the church, and delivered the letter. 📬
When the believers read it, they were encouraged and glad. 😊
Judas and Silas, who were prophets, encouraged and strengthened the believers with many words. 💪
After spending some time there, the brothers sent them back in peace to those who had sent them. 🕊️
Paul and Barnabas stayed in Antioch, teaching and sharing the Lord’s message with many others. 📣
Some time later, Paul said to Barnabas, “Let us go back and visit the believers in every city where we shared the Lord’s message. Let us see how they are doing.” 🛤️
Barnabas wanted to take John, also called Mark, along with them. 👣
But Paul did not think they should take him, because Mark had left them in Pamphylia and had not continued with them in the work. ⚖️
Their disagreement became so sharp that they separated. Barnabas took Mark and sailed to Cyprus, 🌊
but Paul chose Silas and left after the believers entrusted him to the Lord’s grace. 🙏
He traveled through Syria and Cilicia, strengthening the churches. 💪
Paul came to Derbe and then Lystra. A disciple named Timothy was there. His mother was a Jewish believer, and his father was Greek.
The believers in Lystra and Iconium spoke well of Timothy.
Paul wanted Timothy to travel with him, so he circumcised him because of the Jews in that area, who all knew his father was Greek.
As they traveled through the cities, they passed on the decisions the apostles and elders in Jerusalem had made for the believers to follow.
So the churches grew stronger in the faith and increased in number every day.
They traveled through the region of Phrygia and Galatia because the Holy Spirit stopped them from speaking the word in Asia.
When they reached the border of Mysia, they tried to go into Bithynia, but the Spirit of Jesus wouldn’t let them.
So they passed by Mysia and went down to Troas.
During the night Paul saw a vision: a man from Macedonia was standing there, begging him, “Come over to Macedonia and help us!”
After Paul saw the vision, we immediately prepared to leave for Macedonia. We concluded that God had called us to announce the Good News to them.
We sailed from Troas and went straight to Samothrace. The next day we reached Neapolis,
and from there Philippi, a leading city in that part of Macedonia and a Roman colony. We stayed in the city for several days.
On the Sabbath we went outside the city gate to the riverside, where we thought there might be a place of prayer. We sat down and spoke with the women who had gathered there.
One of them was Lydia, a seller of purple cloth from Thyatira who worshiped God. As she listened to Paul, the Lord opened her heart to receive his message.
After Lydia and her household were baptized, she urged us, “If you consider me a faithful believer in the Lord, come stay at my home.” She persuaded us to go.
One day as we were going to the place of prayer, a slave girl with a fortune-telling spirit met us. Her predictions made a lot of money for her owners.
She followed Paul and the rest of us, shouting, “These men serve the Most High God and are telling you how to be saved!”
She kept doing this for many days. Finally Paul, very annoyed, turned to the spirit and said, “In the name of Jesus Christ, I command you to come out of her!” The spirit came out at once.
When her owners realized their chance to make money was gone, they grabbed Paul and Silas and dragged them into the marketplace before the city officials.
They brought them to the magistrates and said, “These men are Jews and they’re stirring up our city.
“They’re promoting customs that we Romans aren’t allowed to accept or practice.”
The crowd joined in against Paul and Silas. The magistrates ordered their clothes torn off and commanded that they be beaten with rods.
After they had beaten them severely, they threw them into prison and ordered the jailer to guard them carefully.
The jailer followed the order, put them in the inner cell, and secured their feet in stocks.
Around midnight Paul and Silas were praying and singing hymns to God while the other prisoners listened.
Suddenly a powerful earthquake shook the prison foundations. All the doors flew open, and everyone’s chains came loose.
The jailer woke up and saw the prison doors open. Thinking the prisoners had escaped, he drew his sword and was about to kill himself.
But Paul shouted, “Don’t hurt yourself! We’re all here!”
The jailer called for lights, rushed in, and trembling, fell down in front of Paul and Silas.
Then he brought them outside and asked, “Sirs, what do I need to do to be saved?”
They answered, “Believe in the Lord Jesus, and you will be saved—you and your household.”
Then they shared the Lord’s message with him and everyone in his home.
At that hour of the night, the jailer took them and washed their wounds. Then he and everyone in his household were baptized right away.
He brought them into his home and served them a meal. He and his whole household were filled with joy because they had come to believe in God.
When morning came, the magistrates sent their officers with the order, “Release those men.”
The jailer told Paul, “The magistrates have ordered you released. You can leave now and go in peace.”

But Paul told the officers, “They beat us in public without a trial, even though we are Roman citizens, and threw us in prison. And now they want to send us away quietly? No. Let them come themselves and escort us out.”
The officers reported this to the magistrates. When they heard that Paul and Silas were Roman citizens, they became afraid.
They came and apologized to them. Then they escorted them out and asked them to leave the city.
After leaving the prison, Paul and Silas went to Lydia’s home. They met with the believers there, encouraged them, and then left.
Paul and his companions traveled through Amphipolis and Apollonia and came to Thessalonica, where there was a Jewish synagogue.
As usual, Paul went in and spent three Sabbaths discussing the Scriptures with them.
He explained and showed that the Messiah had to suffer and rise from the dead. “This Jesus I’m telling you about is the Messiah,” he said.
Some of them were convinced and joined Paul and Silas, along with many devout Greeks and quite a few prominent women.

But the Jews who refused to believe gathered some troublemakers from the marketplace, formed a crowd, and stirred up the city. They attacked Jason’s house, trying to bring Paul and Silas out to the crowd.
When they couldn’t find them, they dragged Jason and some other believers before the city officials, shouting, “These people who have turned the whole world upside down have come here too!
“Jason welcomed them into his home. They’re all defying Caesar’s decrees by saying there is another king—Jesus!”
The crowd and city officials were alarmed when they heard this.
They made Jason and the others post bail, then let them go.
That night the believers sent Paul and Silas to Berea. When they arrived, they went into the Jewish synagogue.
The people there were more open-minded than those in Thessalonica. They eagerly received the message and examined the Scriptures every day to see if it was true.
Many of them believed, including a number of prominent Greek women and men.
But when the Jews in Thessalonica learned that Paul was announcing God’s word in Berea too, they came there and stirred up the crowds.
The believers immediately sent Paul toward the coast, while Silas and Timothy stayed behind.
Those escorting Paul took him as far as Athens. Then they returned with instructions for Silas and Timothy to join him as soon as possible.
While Paul waited for them in Athens, he was deeply troubled to see that the city was full of idols.
He reasoned in the synagogue with Jews and devout Gentiles, and every day in the marketplace with anyone who happened to be there.

Some Epicurean and Stoic philosophers argued with him. Some asked, “What is this talker trying to say?” Others said, “He seems to be promoting foreign gods,” because Paul was announcing Jesus and the resurrection.
They took him to the Areopagus and said, “Can we hear more about this new teaching you’re sharing?
“You’re saying some strange things, and we want to know what they mean.”
All the Athenians and the foreigners living there spent their time talking about or listening to the latest ideas.
Paul stood in the middle of the Areopagus and said, “People of Athens, I can see that you are very religious in every way.
“As I walked around and looked at the things you worship, I even found an altar with this inscription: ‘TO AN UNKNOWN GOD.’ What you worship without knowing, I’m now announcing to you.
“The God who made the world and everything in it is Lord of heaven and earth. He doesn’t live in temples built by human hands.
“He isn’t served by human hands as if he needed anything. He gives everyone life, breath, and everything else.
“From one ancestor he made every nation of people to live across the whole earth. He set their appointed times and the boundaries of where they would live.
“He did this so they might seek God and perhaps reach out for him and find him—though he is never far from any of us.
“For in him we live, move, and exist. As some of your own poets have said, ‘We are also his children.’
“Since we are God’s children, we shouldn’t imagine that God’s nature is like gold, silver, or stone carved by human skill and imagination.
“God overlooked the times when people didn’t know better, but now he commands everyone everywhere to turn back to him.
“He has set a day when he will judge the world fairly through the man he appointed. God has given everyone proof of this by raising him from the dead.”
When they heard about resurrection from the dead, some mocked Paul. Others said, “We want to hear more about this another time.”
Then Paul left the gathering.
But some people joined him and believed. Among them were Dionysius, a member of the Areopagus, a woman named Damaris, and others.
After this, Paul left Athens and went to Corinth.
There he met a Jew named Aquila, originally from Pontus, who had recently arrived from Italy with his wife Priscilla. Claudius had ordered all Jews to leave Rome. Paul went to see them,
and because they had the same trade, he stayed and worked with them. They made tents for a living.
Every Sabbath he reasoned in the synagogue, trying to persuade Jews and Greeks.
When Silas and Timothy came down from Macedonia, Paul devoted himself to preaching and testified to the Jews that Jesus is the Messiah.
But they opposed and insulted him. So he shook the dust from his clothes and said, “You are responsible for what happens to you. I’m innocent. From now on, I’ll go to the Gentiles.”
He left the synagogue and went next door to the home of a man named Justus, who worshiped God.
Crispus, the synagogue leader, believed in the Lord, along with his whole household. Many Corinthians who heard Paul also believed and were baptized.
One night the Lord said to Paul in a vision, “Don’t be afraid. Keep speaking; don’t be silent.
“I am with you. No one will attack or harm you, because I have many people in this city.”
Paul stayed there for a year and six months, teaching God’s word among them.
When Gallio was proconsul of Achaia, the Jews joined forces against Paul and brought him before the judgment seat.
They said, “This man is persuading people to worship God in ways that break the law.”
Paul was about to speak, but Gallio told the Jews, “If this were about a serious crime or real wrongdoing, I would hear you out.
“But since this is a dispute about words, names, and your own law, handle it yourselves. I don’t want to judge a case like this.”
Then he drove them away from the judgment seat.
They all grabbed Sosthenes, the synagogue leader, and beat him in front of the judgment seat. Gallio paid no attention.
Paul stayed in Corinth many more days, then said goodbye to the believers and sailed for Syria with Priscilla and Aquila. In Cenchreae he had his head shaved because he was keeping a vow.
They arrived in Ephesus, where Paul left Priscilla and Aquila. He went into the synagogue and reasoned with the Jews.
They asked him to stay longer, but he declined.
As he said goodbye, he told them, “I must keep the coming feast in Jerusalem. I’ll come back to you if God wills.” Then he sailed from Ephesus.
He landed at Caesarea, went up and greeted the church, then went down to Antioch.
After spending some time there, he left and traveled through Galatia and Phrygia, strengthening all the disciples along the way.
A Jew named Apollos, originally from Alexandria, came to Ephesus. He was an eloquent speaker with a strong grasp of the Scriptures.
He had been taught the Lord’s way and spoke about Jesus with spiritual passion and accuracy, though he knew only John’s baptism.
He began speaking boldly in the synagogue. When Priscilla and Aquila heard him, they took him aside and explained God’s way to him more fully.

When Apollos decided to go to Achaia, the believers encouraged him and wrote to the disciples there, asking them to welcome him. When he arrived, he greatly helped those who had believed through grace.
He publicly and powerfully answered the Jews’ arguments, showing from the Scriptures that Jesus is the Messiah.
While Apollos was in Corinth, Paul traveled through the inland regions and came to Ephesus. There he found some disciples.
He asked them, “Did you receive the Holy Spirit when you believed?” They answered, “We haven’t even heard that there is a Holy Spirit.”
He asked, “Then what baptism did you receive?” They replied, “John’s baptism.”
Paul said, “John baptized people as a sign of turning back to God. He told them to believe in the one coming after him—that is, Jesus.”
When they heard this, they were baptized in the name of the Lord Jesus.
When Paul laid his hands on them, the Holy Spirit came upon them. They spoke in other languages and prophesied.
There were about twelve men in all.
Paul went into the synagogue and spoke boldly for three months, discussing and persuading them about God’s Kingdom.

But some became stubborn and refused to believe. They spoke against the Way in front of everyone, so Paul left them. He took the disciples with him and held daily discussions in the lecture hall of Tyrannus.
This went on for two years, so that everyone living in Asia, both Jews and Greeks, heard the Lord’s message.
God performed extraordinary miracles through Paul.
People took cloths and aprons that had touched him to the sick, and their diseases left them and evil spirits came out.
Some traveling Jewish exorcists tried to use the Lord Jesus’ name over people with evil spirits. They said, “I command you by the Jesus Paul preaches.”
Seven sons of a Jewish chief priest named Sceva were doing this.
But the evil spirit answered, “I know Jesus, and I know Paul. Who are you?”
Then the man with the evil spirit jumped on them and overpowered them. They fled from the house naked and wounded.
Everyone in Ephesus, Jews and Greeks alike, heard about this. Fear came over them all, and the name of the Lord Jesus was honored.
Many who had become believers came forward, admitting and describing what they had done.
A number of people who practiced magic brought their books together and burned them in front of everyone. They calculated the value: fifty thousand pieces of silver.
In this way the Lord’s word spread powerfully and kept growing.
After these events, Paul decided in the Spirit to travel through Macedonia and Achaia and then go to Jerusalem. He said, “After I’ve been there, I must also see Rome.”
He sent two of his helpers, Timothy and Erastus, ahead to Macedonia, while he stayed in Asia for a while.
Around that time, a serious disturbance broke out over the Way.
A silversmith named Demetrius made silver shrines of Artemis, bringing in good business for the craftsmen.
He gathered them and other workers in the same trade and said, “Men, you know this work is how we make our living.
“You can see and hear that Paul has persuaded many people, not only here in Ephesus but throughout almost all Asia. He says that handmade gods aren’t really gods.
“There’s a risk our trade will lose its good name. And the temple of the great goddess Artemis could be discredited, with her magnificence brought down—she whom all Asia and the world worship.”
When they heard this, they became furious and shouted, “Great is Artemis of the Ephesians!”
Confusion spread through the whole city. The crowd rushed together into the theater, dragging along Gaius and Aristarchus, Paul’s travel companions from Macedonia.
Paul wanted to go in and address the crowd, but the disciples wouldn’t let him.
Even some Asiarchs who were his friends sent word, urging him not to risk going into the theater.
Some people in the crowd shouted one thing and others another. The meeting was a total mess, and most didn’t even know why they were there.
The Jews pushed Alexander forward from the crowd. He motioned for silence and tried to defend himself to the people.
But when the crowd realized he was a Jew, they all shouted together for about two hours, “Great is Artemis of the Ephesians!”
At last the city clerk quieted the crowd and said, “People of Ephesus, everyone knows that Ephesus is guardian of the temple of great Artemis and of her image that fell from Zeus.
“Since no one can deny this, you should calm down and not do anything rash.
“You brought these men here, but they haven’t robbed temples or insulted our goddess.
“If Demetrius and the craftsmen with him have a case against anyone, the courts are open and there are proconsuls. Let them bring their charges there.
“If you have any other issue, it must be settled in a lawful assembly.
“We’re in danger of being charged with rioting over what happened today. We have no good reason for this gathering, and we won’t be able to explain this disorder.”
After saying this, he dismissed the assembly.
After the uproar ended, Paul sent for the disciples, encouraged them, said goodbye, and left for Macedonia.
He traveled through those regions, giving the believers many words of encouragement, and then came to Greece.
He spent three months there. Just as he was about to sail for Syria, the Jews plotted against him, so he decided to return through Macedonia.
Sopater from Berea, Aristarchus and Secundus from Thessalonica, Gaius from Derbe, Timothy, and Tychicus and Trophimus from Asia went with him.
They went ahead and waited for us in Troas.
After the Festival of Unleavened Bread, we sailed from Philippi and joined them in Troas five days later. We stayed there for seven days.
On the first day of the week, we gathered to break bread. Paul spoke to them and planned to leave the next day. He kept talking until midnight.
